headline: Approved requests for rapid transit and signal priority on Lincoln, Main and Grafton streets, and for WRTA applications for MassDOT transit grants.
summary: A Tufts University professor presented proposed high-frequency bus corridors and public messaging for WRTA services. Members asked about bus frequency, educating school students about buses, and microtransit funding. Two chairman's orders were approved 3-0, and the bus service hearing order was recommended for hold.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the May 21, 2026 meeting, 2-0 with Ojeda absent.
Recommended placing on file the order requesting a WRTA winter weather plan report, 3-0.
Approved the Chairman's Order asking the City Manager to ensure rapid transit and transit signal prioritization on Lincoln St., Main St., and Grafton St., 3-0.
Approved the Chairman's Order asking the City Manager to encourage WRTA to apply for MassDOT and FY26 community transit grant programs, 3-0.
Recommended holding the order on public hearings to encourage WRTA bus service improvements, 3-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Chairperson Councilor Bilotta read the item and moved for a roll call vote to adopt the item. Order adopted on a roll call vote of 2 Yeas and 0 Nays (Ojeda absent)
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be placed on file. Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta brought forth the following Chairman’s Order on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays: “Request City Manager request Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility work with Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) administrators to ensure rapid transit and transit signal prioritization are implemented on Lincoln St., Main St., and Grafton St.”

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta brought forth the following Chairman’s Order on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays: “Request City Manager encourage Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) administrators to apply for the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) Microtransit and Last-Mile Transit Grant Program and Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) Community Transit Grant Program.”
Chairperson Councilor Bilotta moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held. Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays

### 2 . Approval of the Minutes

a. Order - That the City Council Standing Committee of Public Service and Transportation hereby approves the minutes of the Public Service and Transportation Committee meeting on May 21, 2026.

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta read the item and moved for a roll call vote to adopt the item. Order adopted on a roll call vote of 2 Yeas and 0 Nays (Ojeda absent)

### 3 . Miscellaneous

a. Report of the Committee on Public Service and Transportation Upon the Order of Councilor Sarai Rivera and Councilor Khrystian E. King - Request Standing Committee on Public Service and Transportation meet with the WRTA Administrator to provide City Council with a report concerning the WRTA’s winter weather plan, especially including information as to how snow will be removed at each of the bus stops. # 11e Tuesday, January 27, 2026

In Committee May 21, 2026 - Held

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta read the item and recognized Deputy Administrator and Chief Financial Officer for the WRTA, who provided an overview of the WRTA’s snow operations plan for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27), which included snow removal at all twenty-seven (27) WRTA owned bus shelters, snow removal at eighteen (18) bus stops in the Central Business District, and annual contract agreements for four (4) or more inches of snow fall removal.

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta discussed the twenty-seven (27) bus shelter locations with the Director of Transit Operations and Planning for the WRTA.

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Ojeda, who spoke concerning the process

## used to remove snow at bus shelters and the process to report bus shelters that snow was not removed from with the Deputy Administrator and Chief Financial Officer for the WRTA.

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be placed on file.

## Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays

b. Order of Councilor Gary Rosen, Councilor Robert A. Bilotta, Councilor Morris A. Bergman and Councilor Khrystian E. King - Request Standing Committee on Public Service and Transportation hold public hearings, and later make recommendations, encouraging the Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) to improve bus service to the city’s residents and businesses. Potential considerations for improvements should include, but not be limited to, the implementation of rapid transit, route changes, a same day paratransit pilot program, improved service times, a review of the desirability of their hub and spoke operations and improved metrics. Participants invited to said hearings should include, but not be limited to, local bus transit riders, the WRTA Administrator and the Chairman of their advisory Board, representatives from the Zero Fare Worcester Coalition, the local Riders Action Council, faculty and students in the Department of Urban and Environmental Policy and Planning at Tufts University, the city’s Department of Transportation and Mobility, the city's Commission on Accessibility, the Worcester Department of Public Health, the statewide Transportation for Massachusetts (T4MA) agency, MassDOT and the State Delegation.

# 13b Tuesday, January 13, 2026

## In Committee March 26, 2026 - Held In Committee May 21, 2026 - Held

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta read the item and recognized the Professor of Urban and Environmental Policy and Planning at Tufts University, who provided an overview of the Real Rapid Transit Coalition’s recommendations for the WTRA to implement a high-frequency corridor concept which would include prioritizing the blue corridor (District 3) service stop frequency, adopting a corridor-based service to plan service stops which includes expanding the number of high-frequency corridors, and to increase advertisements and public messaging for such services.

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta discussed locations in the city that provide services more than every thirty (30) minutes with the Professor of Urban and Environmental Policy and Planning at Tufts University and Students at Tufts University.

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Fresolo, who spoke concerning the need for increased public messaging to promote WTRA services and shared bus routes within corridors with the Professor of Urban and Environmental Policy and Planning at Tufts University and Students at Tufts University.

Chairperson Councilor Bilotta discussed the lack of high-frequency corridors traveling west in the city and highlighted the importance of educating Worcester Public School (WPS) students of

## WTRA services with the Professor of Urban and Environmental Policy and Planning at Tufts University.

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Ojeda, who discussed the feasibility of prioritizing bus routes in the vicinity of WPS schools, plans outlined in the city’s Mobility Action Plan to increase public transportation use and to mitigate congested traffic for bus travel, and the importance relative to educating WPS students how to understand and navigate WRTA bus routes with the Professor of Urban and Environmental Policy and Planning at Tufts University and Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility.

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed the frequency in which WRTA buses reach the farthest stops in each corridor with the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and Director of Transit Operations and Planning for the WRTA.

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta brought forth the following Chairman’s Order on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays: “Request City Manager request Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility work with Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) administrators to ensure rapid transit and transit signal prioritization are implemented on Lincoln St., Main St., and Grafton St.”

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta recognized Councilor Ojeda, who spoke concerning feasible on demand transit service options to improve service frequency and access with the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and Speaker #2.

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta discussed potential funding sources to improve microtransit services with Speaker #2 and Speaker #4.

## Chairperson Councilor Bilotta brought forth the following Chairman’s Order on a roll call vote of

3 Yeas and 0 Nays: “Request City Manager encourage Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) administrators to apply for the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) Microtransit and Last-Mile Transit Grant Program and Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) Community Transit Grant Program.”

- Chairperson Councilor Bilotta moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held.

Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
